etymologies.etymologyHTML: From door +‎ way.

definitions.definition: The passage of a door; a door-shaped entrance into a house or a room.

quote.citation: 1950 February, “Rolling Stock for London Transport”, in Railway Magazine, page 88:
quote.text: A re-arrangement of the seating in relation to doorway positions gives an even distribution of seated passengers, no change has been made in the number or size of the doorways.

definitions.definition: (figuratively) An opening or passage in general.

quote.citation: 1850, [Alfred, Lord Tennyson], In Memoriam, London: Edward Moxon, […], →OCLC, Canto XLIII, page 66:
quote.text: How fares it with the happy dead?For here the man is more and more;⁠But he forgets the days beforeGod shut the doorways of his head [i.e. the sutures of the skull].
